hook.text: Say every word twice twice. You just decoded that sentence despite the error. Redundancy saved you.

buildup.text: Adding redundancy means sending extra bits that carry no new information but help detect or fix errors.

discovery.text: The simplest approach: send each bit three times. Majority vote corrects any single-bit flip.

twist.text: Triple repetition wastes 2/3 of bandwidth. Good codes add far less redundancy and correct far more errors.

climax.text: The art of coding is finding the minimum redundancy needed for the maximum error correction. Shannon set the bound.

punchline.text: Extra bits now, fewer errors later. That's the deal.

quiz.question: What is the tradeoff of adding redundancy for error correction?
options: Lower bandwidth efficiency for higher reliability
